summary: Okta RelayState parameter stripped on 302 via corp VPN -> SSO redirect causes support-portal login loop
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users are unable to complete SSO login to the Support Portal when connected over the corporate VPN. Behavior is an apparent redirect loop back to the Support Portal (no active session), even though Okta shows an authenticated assertion.

Impact: ~12 engineers and oncall responders using prod-us-east are unable to access the internal Support Portal or escalate tickets via the web UI. Affects oncall rotation for the afternoon shift; potential missed paging.

Observed behavior: Okta successful SAML assertion is recorded, but the final SP session is not established. Browser shows a 302 from our auth-proxy to the support portal with Location header lacking RelayState (or the RelayState query param is empty). The portal rejects the login because SP expects original RelayState to map back to pending request, resulting in immediate redirect back to Okta.

Environment details: Issue reproduces when users are on corporate VPN (split-tunnel disabled) with device-attestation enabled. Users not on VPN are not affected. Affected clients include Chrome v117 and Firefox v117 on macOS and Ubuntu.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect to corporate VPN (split tunnel disabled) on a managed device.
2) Navigate to https://support.redwood.ai and click "Sign in with SSO".
3) Okta auth flow completes (MFA/passkeys) and Okta redirects back to https://auth-proxy.redwood.ai/saml/consume with a 302 to the SP.
4) Observe that the Location header on the 302 does not contain RelayState (or contains RelayState=). The browser then navigates back to https://support.redwood.ai without session, triggering another login.

Logs / evidence:
- Okta system logs: user.auth.saml.sso success entries present for affected users, with Response ID X and InResponseTo Y.
- auth-proxy logs (prod-us-east, nov-02 14:12 UTC): 302 emitted to support portal with "Location: https://support.redwood.ai" (no RelayState).
- edge-proxy access logs show an internal rewrite rule applied for requests coming from the VPN egress IP range (10.24.0.0/18).
- Browser devtools capture attached by user (console output pasted into comments).

Temporary workaround: Users can disable the corporate VPN (use mobile hotspot) to complete SSO, or use an SSH jump host to access internal console until fix is applied.

Recommended priority: P1 given impact on oncall workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: Connect to corporate VPN with managed device (split-tunnel disabled)
Open browser to https://support.redwood.ai and click Sign in with SSO
Observe redirect back to auth-proxy and final 302 to support portal missing RelayState parameter leading to login loop
comments: 2024-11-02 14:30 - Asha Patel (reporter): Collected two HARs from affected users (attached) and a screenshot of Okta success entry. Users confirm they only hit the problem when on corp VPN.

2024-11-02 15:05 - Luca Moreno (assignee): Reproduced locally by simulating VPN egress using the same subnet. Confirmed the 302 location header is different when request path traverses edge-proxy rule-set A. Adding diagnostic logs to auth-proxy to dump location header before emit.

2024-11-02 17:20 - SRE (Maya Chen): Edge-proxy team rolled a rewrite change last week (PR #1842) that normalizes query params for certain egress ranges. Suspect this normalizer is stripping empty or duplicate RelayState on 302s. Filed PR revert candidate.

2024-11-03 09:12 - Identity (Rajiv Singh): Okta logs show InResponseTo present; the SP decryption and assertion mapping succeed server-side but session creation fails due to missing RelayState key in session store lookup. Session store expects a non-empty RelayState token previously recorded in auth-proxy state.
investigation_notes: Auth-proxy emits session mapping using RelayState as lookup key; if missing the flow is treated as unsolicited and rejected.
Edge-proxy rewrite applied to queries from VPN egress range strips parameters that match pattern 'relay*' because of a legacy param-scrub list used to prevent cache poisoning.
Reproduced in staging by forcing incoming IP into the VPN CIDR; 302s from auth-proxy lost RelayState only when passed through edge rewrite stage.
Related config: /etc/edge-proxy/param_scrub.conf contains 'relay*' entry since 2024-10-18 change (PR 1842).
Auth-proxy debug dump: original Redirect location computed correctly with RelayState=abc123, but after edge-proxy rewrite the outbound TCP stream shows Location header lacking query string.
resolution_notes: 2024-11-03 12:00 - Rolled back edge-proxy PR 1842 from prod-us-east; verified RelayState preserved in 302 Location headers for VPN-ejected flows.
2024-11-03 12:14 - Performed coordinated smoke test with three affected users on VPN; all successfully completed SSO and established portal sessions.

2024-11-03 13:00 - Edge-proxy team prepared follow-up PR 1847 which replaces the blunt 'relay*' scrub with an allowlist for known safe params and adds explicit handling for RelayState. Planning staged rollout to prod-us-east after validation in staging.

Follow-up actions: (1) Add unit/integration test to edge-proxy to ensure RelayState preserved across rewrites; (2) Add observability metric for missing RelayState on SAML consume paths; (3) Notify security that param scrub rules were modified and validated to avoid reintroducing cache-poisoning exposure.
resolution_status: Partial fix deployed (edge-proxy revert); permanent fix in review
followup_tasks: EDGE-1847: replace relay* scrub with allowlist and explicit RelayState passthrough - in review
AUTH-210: add metric for missing RelayState in SAML flows
SEC-322: review param-scrub policy and document exceptions
notes_for_customer_or_internal_users: If you see the login loop and are on corp VPN, temporarily disconnect from VPN or use an alternate network. If you must remain on VPN, contact SRE in #support and include timestamp (UTC) for tracing.
